basis: Osteolysis, arthropathy and subcutaneous nodulosis define the supplied MMP14-related MONA concept; gingival findings lack a qualifying frequency.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: subcutaneous nodulosis is a defining component of the supplied disease concept; hirsutism alone would not justify this axis.

basis: Unresolved legacy protocadherin entry without a defined disease phenotype; no organ assignment is supported. Requires ontology review.

decisions.neurologic: none: a protocadherin name does not establish neurologic disease; no definition, clinical phenotype or informative disease ancestor supports it.

basis: Larval tissue invasion causes characteristic hepatic inflammation and frequent pneumonitis; both are in the disease definition. Reactive eosinophilia is not blood-organ damage.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: frequent pneumonitis is explicitly part of the defining visceral larval disease, alongside hepatomegaly.

basis: An inherited coenzyme A biosynthesis disorder causes progressive brain neurodegeneration. Retinopathy, blindness and optic atrophy occur in only 1-4% of the atypical form.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: pantothenate kinase deficiency is an inborn defect of coenzyme A metabolism, so the metabolic mechanism axis applies.

basis: Skeletal defects and severe CNS disease characterize the syndrome; sparse hair 26/27 and nail hypoplasia 22/24 support skin involvement. Isolated cardiac reports lack cohort prevalence.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: tetralogy in 1/1 assessed is an isolated report, not evidence that cardiac defects affect at least 30% of the syndrome population.
decisions.neurologic: primary: severe CNS disease is a defining feature, including neuronal loss and brain malformations. [FIG4 study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3644641/)

basis: Vitamin D metabolic defect with defining rickets; cardiomyopathy and hypochromic anemia each have HPO frequency 30-79%. Aminoaciduria alone does not establish direct renal injury.

decisions.haematologic: involved: hypochromic anemia represents blood-cell dysfunction and is annotated frequent (30-79%); no separate cause is established in this record.
decisions.renal: none: aminoaciduria (80-99%) alone does not establish direct kidney injury or clinically significant tubular failure from this disease.

basis: HPO: strabismus and dental defects 30-79%; ASD 7/10 and PDA 30-79%. Hearing loss 10/42 is below threshold; minor limb morphology alone does not establish locomotor damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: dental defects are frequent (30-79% HPO), with impacted or absent teeth and abnormal decay reported. [GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK603087/)

basis: Cutaneous and visceral vascular tumors; hepatic involvement in most, anemia/coagulopathy 80-99% in HPO. Renal insufficiency, also annotated 80-99%, is omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: thrombocytopenia, anemia and coagulation abnormalities are annotated 80-99%; substantial consumptive blood dysfunction merits priority under the cap.
decisions.renal: none under cap: renal insufficiency is annotated 80-99%, but defining vascular/skin disease, predominant hepatic tumors and severe blood dysfunction take priority.

basis: Parent BWS supports defining somatic overgrowth, macroglossia and abdominal-wall defects. Hypoglycemia is usually transient; persistent subtype-specific endocrine damage is unproven.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: parent BWS hypoglycemia (~30-50%) is usually transient; persistent dysfunction is unproven in this subtype. [GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1394/)

basis: Exogenous glucocorticoid excess defines the endocrine syndrome. Additional steroid-induced skin, muscle and bone effects are excluded by the explicit treatment-effect rule.

decisions.dermatologic: none: skin atrophy and striae can be common, but in this exogenous syndrome they result from corticosteroid treatment and fail the treatment-effect exclusion.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: steroid myopathy and bone loss can be common, but are effects of corticosteroid treatment and fail the treatment-effect exclusion.
